claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation can form a thin, continuous alumina surface layer on a boride-based component.
A pre-formed alumina layer will improve the boride-based component's resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
Exposure to a controlled oxygen environment at elevated temperature induces formation of a protective alumina scale on the component.
There are temperatures that favor alumina formation without excessive oxidation of the bulk boride material.
The alumina scale can remain adherent and chemically stable in an oxygen-lean molten-aluminum bath at hot-dip plating temperatures.
The pre-oxidation treatment produces a thin, dense, and adherent alumina layer.
Alumina can act as a diffusion barrier.
The alumina layer separates molten aluminum from the boride substrate.
The pre-formed alumina scale hinders direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying boride.
Hindering contact between molten aluminum and the boride reduces elemental dissolution.
The alumina barrier slows molten-aluminum corrosion kinetics.
Pre-oxidized components will have significantly lower mass loss than untreated components after immersion in molten aluminum.
Pre-oxidized components will have significantly less surface degradation than untreated components after immersion in molten aluminum.
Untreated boride-based components typically experience relatively high molten-aluminum corrosion because they lack a protective barrier and are directly exposed to the melt.
Loss of alumina-scale integrity compromises its protective effect.
Extreme operating temperatures, strongly reducing environments, or mechanical wear may disrupt the alumina scale and reduce protection.
